title: No More Aging Phone: Camera, PTZ and Stick Guard Stay Up | vitalii.no
description:
One old phone on a shelf was the single point of failure for a home camera, PTZ control, and two tunnels back to the cloud — not anymore.

The TV stick guard, the camera frame relay, PTZ control, and the reverse SSH tunnels back to an Oracle cloud VM all depended on one old Samsung XCover phone running Termux on a shelf at home. A battery drain, a forced reboot, or one dropped Wi-Fi handshake was enough to silently take the whole home-monitoring chain down, and nobody noticed until the camera feed went dark.

A 311-line Python script, using only the standard library, now runs as a Windows Scheduled Task under the SYSTEM account on the always-on home PC. It uploads camera frames to Cloudflare R2, relays PTZ commands, serves on-demand snapshots, and opens two reverse SSH tunnels to the Oracle VM, one for camera RTSP and one for the PC's own sshd, taking over everything the phone used to carry.

The home PC restarts the whole bridge itself on every reboot, and all four services, guard, frames, PTZ, and tunnels, now stay alive without anyone having to check on a phone running Termux.
